 Jaden McDaniels keeps proving the Timberwolves right for viewing him as untouchable 
 You don't trade players like this. By Eamon Cassels | Nov 18, 2026, 3:44 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Minnesota Timberwolves forward Jaden McDaniels (Photo by Carlos Gonzalez/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) | Star Tribune via Getty Images During the offseason, the Minnesota Timberwolves made Jaden McDaniels untouchable , including in trade talks for Giannis Antetokounmpo. He has long been labeled "virtually untouchable." 
--> During the offseason, the Minnesota Timberwolves made Jaden McDaniels untouchable , including in trade talks for Giannis Antetokounmpo. He has long been labeled "virtually untouchable." 
 This season, McDaniels is showing why the Timberwolves were right to believe in him so much. Through 15 games, McDaniels is averaging 17.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. He's a big reason why the Wolves are off to an 11-4 start, and he's been arguably the team's most consistent player. 
--> This season, McDaniels is showing why the Timberwolves were right to believe in him so much. Through 15 games, McDaniels is averaging 17.1 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. He's a big reason why the Wolves are off to an 11-4 start, and he's been arguably the team's most consistent player. 
 McDaniels had a career-best season last year, averaging 14.8 points, and now, with more consistent involvement, he's leveled up again. Due to his elite on-ball defense, McDaniels was already an immensely valuable player, but now that he's an elite third scoring option, it's easy to see why the Timberwolves view him so highly. 
--> McDaniels had a career-best season last year, averaging 14.8 points, and now, with more consistent involvement, he's leveled up again. Due to his elite on-ball defense, McDaniels was already an immensely valuable player, but now that he's an elite third scoring option, it's easy to see why the Timberwolves view him so highly. 
 This isn't the first time in the past year that McDaniels has backed up the Wolves' belief in him. He was labeled as virtually untouchable last season, and his incredible two-way play in the postseason, including a 32-point showing in Game 6 of the first-round, made it clear why the Wolves valued him so much. 
--> This isn't the first time in the past year that McDaniels has backed up the Wolves' belief in him. He was labeled as virtually untouchable last season, and his incredible two-way play in the postseason, including a 32-point showing in Game 6 of the first-round, made it clear why the Wolves valued him so much. 
 Jaden McDaniels' stellar two-way impact makes him indispensable to the Timberwolves
--> Jaden McDaniels' stellar two-way impact makes him indispensable to the Timberwolves
 Title teams aren't only built around All-Stars. Of course, you need at least one (the Wolves at full strength have two). Still, you need players who can complement stars and scale up when needed. McDaniels does exactly that. 
--> Title teams aren't only built around All-Stars. Of course, you need at least one (the Wolves at full strength have two). Still, you need players who can complement stars and scale up when needed. McDaniels does exactly that. 
 He makes life easier for Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball by taking on tough matchups. Notably, McDaniels ranks in the 88th percentile for matchup difficulty according to CraftedNBA. And McDaniels doesn't just guard opposing stars—he shuts them down. 
--> He makes life easier for Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball by taking on tough matchups. Notably, McDaniels ranks in the 88th percentile for matchup difficulty according to CraftedNBA. And McDaniels doesn't just guard opposing stars—he shuts them down. 
 McDaniels is holding opposing players to 41.3 percent from the field as the primary defender. The most recent example of him taking a star out of games is how he held Damian Lillard to 4-for-13 shooting in back-to-back games against the Portland Trail Blazers. In a playoff setting, having a defensive stopper like McDaniels who can genuinely limit star players is a massive advantage. 
--> McDaniels is holding opposing players to 41.3 percent from the field as the primary defender. The most recent example of him taking a star out of games is how he held Damian Lillard to 4-for-13 shooting in back-to-back games against the Portland Trail Blazers. In a playoff setting, having a defensive stopper like McDaniels who can genuinely limit star players is a massive advantage. 
 That's not a player you trade when you have title aspirations. Look at what OG Anunoby did for the New York Knicks during their title run—that's the type of advantage Minnesota has with McDaniels. 
--> That's not a player you trade when you have title aspirations. Look at what OG Anunoby did for the New York Knicks during their title run—that's the type of advantage Minnesota has with McDaniels. 
 While McDaniels has long been an elite defender, it's truly his offensive growth that has solidified his untouchable status. A lot of his offensive skill set is complementary. Edwards and LaMelo draw tougher matchups, which leads teams to hide their weak defenders on McDaniels. Thankfully, he can punish these mismatches at an elite level. 
--> While McDaniels has long been an elite defender, it's truly his offensive growth that has solidified his untouchable status. A lot of his offensive skill set is complementary. Edwards and LaMelo draw tougher matchups, which leads teams to hide their weak defenders on McDaniels. Thankfully, he can punish these mismatches at an elite level. 
 On certain nights, McDaniels can score at a star level as a self-creator. We saw this on Tuesday when he scored 22 points against the Blazers. McDaniels' ability to get to the rim and his spots in the mid-range help him create offense for himself at a consistent and efficient rate. 
--> On certain nights, McDaniels can score at a star level as a self-creator. We saw this on Tuesday when he scored 22 points against the Blazers. McDaniels' ability to get to the rim and his spots in the mid-range help him create offense for himself at a consistent and efficient rate. 
 Consistency has been what has impressed me most about McDaniels' season. While McDaniels leveled up last season, he still had occasional duds. So far this season, though, McDaniels has scored at least 13 points in every single game. 
--> Consistency has been what has impressed me most about McDaniels' season. While McDaniels leveled up last season, he still had occasional duds. So far this season, though, McDaniels has scored at least 13 points in every single game. 
 Credit to the Wolves not just for believing in him, but for consistently empowering him as a creator and drawing up plays for him. Yes, Edwards' unfortunate injury opened up opportunities for him, but even before his injury, McDaniels was regularly involved in the offense. 
--> Credit to the Wolves not just for believing in him, but for consistently empowering him as a creator and drawing up plays for him. Yes, Edwards' unfortunate injury opened up opportunities for him, but even before his injury, McDaniels was regularly involved in the offense. 
 Look, McDaniels will likely never be an All-Star (though I don't think he's that far off), and he's not a top-10 player in the league. However, his impact on winning is undeniable. Having a defensive stopper, mismatch punisher, and complementary creator all wrapped up into one is beyond valuable. 
--> Look, McDaniels will likely never be an All-Star (though I don't think he's that far off), and he's not a top-10 player in the league. However, his impact on winning is undeniable. Having a defensive stopper, mismatch punisher, and complementary creator all wrapped up into one is beyond valuable. 
 Players like McDaniels don't grow on trees. And while the Wolves could've traded him for a more talented player, you couldn't find a better fit alongside star players than McDaniels. That's why the Timberwolves were determined to keep McDaniels at all costs, and he keeps proving them right.
